Independent probe, tests/nexus/zz_10T3_probe.test.ts (deleted afterwards). It walks every export of every src/data/*.ts, counting every numeric leaf inside any shape (objects, arrays, mixed tuples, typed arrays) and whether an ancestor record or a ..._STATUS export gives a status. Numeric leaves and uncovered ones: batteries 60/0, constants 25/3, constituents 313/0, disciplines 0/0, materials 769/1, mixes 28/24, motors 42/0, optics 3321/0, periodic 530/0, references 0/0, woods 6/0. The 4 uncovered in constants.ts and materials.ts are STANDARD_GRAVITY, SIGMA_SB and FARADAY, bare aliases of values in the statused CONSTANTS record. The 24 in mixes.ts are real figures with no status: MIXES['concrete-c25'].parts (4 kg values in [id, kg] pairs) and the phase fractions of 9 of the 11 MIXTURES records (cfrp-ud-60, gfrp-random-30, gfrp-woven-50, al-sic-20, thermal-paste-60, concrete-aggregate-70, pa66-gf30, fr4, concrete-c25; 20 fractions). Only glass-wool and al-foam-10 carry a status. The scan returns [] for all of them, which is why the test passes. The gap is in the scan, not only in the data: the scan's `figure` does not count a [name, number] pair as a figure, so a record whose figures all sit in such pairs is never asked for a status.

A bare numeric export with no source and no status (planted H) is invisible to both unsourced and unstated, because the walker returns on any non-object top-level value. The real aliases (STANDARD_GRAVITY, SIGMA_SB, FARADAY) copy statused constants, so no real figure is lost today, but the check would pass whatever a new bare figure said. Needed: treat a numeric export as a figure needing a status and a source, or say plainly that it is not covered.
